decisions.title: What counts as a duplicate?
decisions.body: Two files are duplicates when... exact byte match only, or also perceptual near-matches (re-encodes, resizes, light edits)? This decides what the tool can safely automate downstream.

options.text: Exact content hash only (SHA-256 of bytes)
pcr: Zero false positives; every match is provably the same file
Misses every re-encode and resized export, which may be most of the waste
Downstream deletion can be fully automatic because a match is a certainty

options.text: Perceptual hash (pHash/dHash) with a similarity threshold, plus exact hash
pcr: Catches re-encodes, resizes and near-identical bursts
False positives are possible, so no match can be trusted blindly; needs a threshold and a review step
Downstream handling can no longer auto-delete; the index must store perceptual hashes and a similarity structure

decisions.title: What happens to a duplicate once found?
decisions.body: Given a group of files judged duplicates, what does the tool do with the extras? The premise of this question is that a match is certain enough to act on automatically.

options.text: Move extras to a dated quarantine folder on the NAS; purge on a later explicit command
pcr: Every action is reversible until the owner purges
Quarantine consumes the space it was meant to free until purged
Needs a purge command and a policy for how long quarantine lives

options.text: Replace extras with hardlinks to the kept original
pcr: Space reclaimed immediately, paths all still resolve
Editing one path edits all; irreversible in practice once files diverge
Requires the NAS filesystem to support hardlinks across the scanned tree

options.text: Report only; never touch a file
pcr: Cannot lose anything
Reclaims nothing by itself; the owner does the work by hand
Makes a keep-rule and a purge policy unnecessary

decisions.title: Which copy in a group is the one kept?
decisions.body: When several files match, one survives. Pick by what? This assumes the group is a set of true equals, so the only question is which path is the original.

options.text: Oldest modification time wins; ties broken by shortest path
pcr: Usually the original import
Wrong when a backup restore reset mtimes
Deterministic; the same scan always keeps the same file

options.text: Prefer the copy under a configured 'originals' root, else oldest
pcr: Respects the owner's own organisation
Needs configuration before first run
A file outside any originals root falls back to the mtime rule

decisions.title: Where does the scan index live?
decisions.body: Hashing 200k files takes hours. Where is the result stored so the next run is incremental, and what does it need to hold? This assumes a simple hash-to-path map is enough.

options.text: SQLite file at the NAS root, keyed by path with size, mtime and hash
pcr: Incremental re-scans skip unchanged files by size+mtime
One more file on the NAS the owner must not delete
Easy to extend with more columns later

options.text: No index; full re-hash every run
pcr: Nothing to corrupt or keep in sync
Hours per run, every run
Rules out any feature that needs history, such as quarantine ageing

mootness.answer: Perceptual hash (pHash/dHash) with a similarity threshold, plus exact hash
